Footer Bar

The site footer bar: company menu, review badges, brand and address, socials, partner logos and the legal line. It sits below Product Footer — the two stack, they do not replace each other.

3 of 3 variants3 bands1440 · 768 · 390◆ Dark onlyFigma 877:2953

Default

Figma’s Property 1=Default. The menu row and the brand row are both --color-bg-footer-alt; only the legal row underneath is --color-bg-footer — the opposite way round to what the token names suggest.

The panel animates with grid-template-rows: 0fr → 1fr, so it opens to whatever height its own content needs — no measured max-height to go stale when a link is added. Each column then rises in turn, and prefers-reduced-motion collapses all of it to a cut. Collapsed, the panel carries inert: it stays in the DOM to animate, and inert is what stops it from holding focus while it is closed.

Responsive

Figma draws footer-md (768) and footer-sm (390) as separate symbols. They are mapped onto this project’s own breakpoints — --breakpoint-lg 1024 and --breakpoint-md 768 — so the wide layout holds down to 1024, md covers 768–1023 and sm everything below. Those numbers are written out in the @media conditions rather than read from the tokens, because a custom property in a media query condition never matches.
Each preview below is an <iframe> loading this same page at ?frame=, because an iframe is the only thing on a page with a viewport of its own — the demo frames above are pinned to 1440 and will never show these. Nothing is duplicated to make them work.
768px
Drag the handle, or use the presets — the readout names the layout you are looking at, and the frame reports its own height back so nothing is a guessed number. The handle takes arrow keys too (±16, or ±1 with Shift), which is worth having: dragging to find the exact pixel where a layout flips is how you check a breakpoint landed where you meant it to. The menu drops its per-item padding for a flat 12px gap and wraps — two rows at 768, three at 390, matching Figma’s wrap points exactly. A divider that ends a row is hidden, so no row trails a separator into nothing; the space it takes stays, which is what keeps the wrap where Figma puts it. The Free tools panel has no frame to match: its groups stack, and inside each one the design’s editorial column breaks stay intact while auto-fill decides how many sit per row — 4 at 768, 2 at 390, 1 at 320.

Token Reference

This component is the first consumer either footer background token has ever had. Both were imported with the colour ramp and sat unread until now.

Props

Read from interface Props in FooterBar.astro, so it cannot drift from the component.
PropTypeDefaultNotes
menuLink[]8 itemsThe links along the top row, each { label, href? }.
freeToolsbooleanfalseShows the Free Tools item in the menu, before Webinars.
freeToolsLabelstring'Free tools'The Free Tools item's text.
freeToolsHrefstring—Where the Free Tools item links when there is no panel — with toolGroups it is a button that opens one instead.
toolGroupsToolGroup[]3 itemsThe panel the Free Tools item opens: groups of links, each with a title, an icon and its columns.
toolsOpenbooleanfalseRender the panel already open.
closeToolsLabelstring'Close free tools'Accessible name for the panel's close button, which shows only an icon.
reviewsReview[]2 itemsThe review scores — logo, stars and score for each site.
addressstring'205 N. Michigan Ave. Chicago, IL 60611 USA +1 (312) 252-3088'The postal address and phone number under the logo.
socialsSocial[]5 itemsThe social icons, each { name, icon, href? }; name is the link's accessible name.
messageLabelstring'Message us on:'The text before the messaging icons.
messengersMessenger[]2 itemsThe messaging channels after the label, each { name, icon, href? }; name is the link's accessible name.
partnersPartner[]3 itemsThe partner logos, each with the width it is drawn at.
copyrightstring'Copyright © Iron Software 2013-2026'The copyright line in the bottom row.
legalLink[]4 itemsThe legal links in the bottom row, with a divider between each.
donateLabelstring'Every Iron Suite Donates'The text beside the 1% for the Planet logo.
donateImgstring'1% logo - Horizontal.png'The 1% for the Planet logo's file name, inside basePath.
basePathstring'assets'The folder every image and icon is loaded from.
classstring—Extra classes on the <footer>, after the component's own.
